extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of Milton, literary history, and history of censorship
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted standards and rules (primarily the 1637 Star Chamber Decree and related historical censorship practices) governing printing, licensing, importation, and punishment in early modern England and continental precedents. Useful for understanding legal/regulatory controls on publication and the historical context of Milton's Areopagitica.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to seize unlicensed printed materials and apprehend persons involved
rubrics_metrics.description: Order to seize and carry away printed or reprinted materials produced by those with no lawful interest in them and to apprehend all authors, printers, and others employed in compiling, printing, stitching, binding, publishing and dispersing scandalous, unlicensed, and unwarrantable papers, books and pamphlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seized items to remain in the Common Hall until either House of Parliament disposes of them; offenders to be brought before either House or the Committee of Examinations to receive further punishment; Justices of the Peace, captains, constables and other officers ordered to aid in execution and to break open doors and locks in case of opposition. (Context: enforcement provision in the Star Chamber Decree quoted in the introduction.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to publish the Order publicly
rubrics_metrics.description: It is further ordered that this Order be forthwith printed and published, to the end that notice may be taken thereof, and all contemners of it left inexcusable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication of the decree itself was mandated so that noncompliance could not be excused by ignorance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papal bull (1501) prohibition until episcopal consultation and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Pope Alexander VI's bull forbade all printers in certain provinces from printing until they had consulted the archbishops, vicars, or officials and obtained their special and express licence; those who printed without such licence faced excommunication and pecuniary fines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bull required examination by 'able and catholic persons' and ordered burning of earlier printed works judged prejudicial to the Catholic religion; demonstrates ecclesiastical-origin censorship precedents cited in the introduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council of Lateran (1515) — ecclesiastical inspection requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lateran Council (1515) ordered that, in future, no books should be printed but such as had been inspected by ecclesiastical censors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An explicit early requirement that printing be preceded by inspection by church authorities; used as background for the historical rise of formal censorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on printing seditious, schismatic or offensive books (Imprimis clause)
rubrics_metrics.description: That no person whatsoever shall presume to print either beyond the seas or in this realm any seditious, scismaticall, or offensive books or pamphlets to the scandal of religion, the Church, the Government, governors of the Church or State, or of any corporation or particular person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offenders were to lose all such books and pamphlets and suffer severe punishment (fine, imprisonment, corporal punishment, or otherwise) as the Court or high Commission shall think fit. This is a central content-based prohibition from the Star Chamber Decree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory licensing and registration with the Company of Stationers (Clause II)
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall print any book or pamphlet unless the book and all titles, epistles, prefaces, proems, preambles, introductions, tables, dedications, and other matters annexed are first lawfully licenced and authorized by specified persons and are entered into the Register Book of the Company of Stationers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty: every printer offending shall be forever disabled to exercise the art of printing and receive further punishment as the courts shall require. Emphasizes both pre-publication licensing and registration requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated licensing authorities by book-type (Clause III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Books concerning the common laws to be printed by special allowance of the Lords Chief Justices or chief baron; books of history or state affairs to be licenced by the principal Secretaries of State; heraldry and titles/arms by the Earl Marshal; all other books (divinity, physic, philosophy, poetry, etc.) to be allowed by the Lord Archbishop of Canterbury or Bishop of London or by Chancellors/Vice-Chancellors of the universities (with provisos).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which office/licensor is responsible for approving particular subject-matter, limiting arbitrary licensing by routing approvals to named authorities; includes proviso that university licensors license only within university limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensors must retain two written copies and certify conformity (Clause IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person appointed to licence books shall have two separate written copies of the same book (including titles, prefaces, etc.); one copy to be kept in the public registries of the Archbishop/Bishop/Chancellor/etc., and the other with the licensor; on both copies the licensor shall testify under hand that there is nothing contrary to Christian faith, Church of England doctrine and discipline, nor against the State or good life and manners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The licence or approbation must be imprinted at the beginning of the book with the name(s) of the licensor as testimony of allowance; the two-copy system was intended to prevent post-licensing alteration and to provide public archival proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on imprinting or importing books where Stationers hold exclusive rights (Clause VII)
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall imprint or import into the kingdom any copy or part of any book printed beyond the seas which the Company of Stationers or any other person have by Letters Patents, Order, or Entrance in their Register book the sole right, privilege, authority, or allowance solely to print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty: forfeiture of the books and fines or other punishment levied by the Court or high Commission as appropriate; protects proprietary/privileged printing rights held by Stationers or patentees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printers must print their names and authors' names on works (Clause VIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person that shall print any books, ballads, charts, portraiture, or other things shall print and set his and their own name or names, as also the name or names of the author or authors, maker or makers of the same, and by or from whom any such book is printed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty: forfeiture of offending items, defacement and disabling of presses, fines, imprisonment, corporal punishment, or other penalties as courts see fit; intended to ensure accountability and traceability of printed materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on foreigners importing and vending books (Clause XII)
rubrics_metrics.description: No stranger or foreigner shall be suffered to bring in or vent any book or books printed beyond the seas, in any language, either by themselves or their secret factors, except free Stationers of London and those brought up in that profession who have their livelihood depending thereupon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty: confiscation of all such books so imported and further penalties as courts shall impose; a protectionist and control measure over foreign-published materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirement before erecting printing-houses (Clause XIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall erect any press or printing-house, nor let or suffer any house, vault, cellar or other room to be used for printing, unless the demiser or lessor first gives notice to the Master and Wardens of the Company of Stationers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty: imprisonment and other punishments as the Court or the high Commission shall think fit; intended to control the proliferation of presses and maintain oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on number of master printers allowed (Clause XV)
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be but twenty Master Printers allowed to have the use of one presse or more; the Court nominates and admits twenty specific persons to have presses; the Archbishop or Bishop with commissioners may supply the places as they fall void, provided they do not exceed twenty besides His Majesty's Printers and university printers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A formal cap on licensed master printers in London to concentrate control over printing; names of those allowed were listed in the Decree.

rubrics_metrics.name: University printers permitted apprentices but limited interactions with London (Clause XXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court does not restrain printers of either of the universities from taking what number of apprentices they think fit; provided that such printers employ all their own journeymen within themselves and not suffer any of them to go abroad for employment to the printers of London (unless specific exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proviso to protect university presses' labour force and restrict their use by London printers; penalties to be inflicted by the Chancellor of either university for delinquents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for Master/Wardens or licensed master-printers to search for unlicensed printing (Clause XXV)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Master and Wardens of the Company of Stationers, or any two licensed Master-Printers appointed by the Archbishop or Bishop, shall have power to take assistance and to search houses and shops (especially printing-houses), at what time they think fit, to view what is in printing, call for the licence to see whether it be licenced or no, and if not to seize so much as is printed together with the offenders and bring them before the Archbishop or Bishop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables self-regulation and policing by the Stationers' Company and licensed master-printers; provides a mechanism for discovery and seizure of unlicensed production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searchers may seize suspected anti-doctrinal books and refer to bishops (Clause XXVI)
rubrics_metrics.description: If upon search they find any book or part of a book which they suspect to contain matter contrary to the doctrine and discipline of the Church of England, or against the State and Government, they may seize such book(s) and bring them to the Archbishop of Canterbury or the Bishop of London for further course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives ecclesiastical authorities the role of adjudicating doctrinally suspect works seized by searchers; emphasizes church/state review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction to four founders of letters for printing (Clause XXVII)
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be four founders of letters for printing allowed, and no more; the Court nominates and admits four persons to be letter-founders for the time being, and the Archbishop or Bishop with commissioners may supply places as they fall void, provided they do not exceed the number of four.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty for unallowed founders: punishment as the Court or High Commission shall think fit; constrains the manufacture of type to approved founders to limit rogue production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to reserve a copy for the university library (Clause XXXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement that one book of every sort that is new printed or reprinted with additions be sent to the University of Oxford for the use of the public library; every printer shall reserve one new book and bring it to the Common Hall of the Company of Stationers to be sent to the library before any public venting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty: imprisonment and further order as the Court or high Commission shall think fit if the printer fails to deliver the reserved copy; an early legal deposit requirement (specifically for Oxford).

rubrics_metrics.name: General punitive and accountability mechanisms throughout the Decree
rubrics_metrics.description: Across clauses: offenders face loss and forfeiture of offending books, defacement and disabling of presses, fines, imprisonment, corporal punishment, confiscation of imported books, and other penalties as determined by the Court or the high Commission Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The repeated threat of severe punishments underpinned enforcement; provisions combine proprietary, doctrinal, and political controls with concrete sanctions and mechanisms for enforcement and record-keeping.
